Sidewalks slanting  for drainage making it a balance risk for me the sidewalks are not level so I end up leaning left or right as I walk making it possible I will fall. Some sidewalks are up against or too far the curb with valleys between which has meant I am picking up or lowering down my walker to navigate sidewalk to curb or vice versa, sometimes I can’t navigate because too steep sidewalk to curb or too big a gap between.  Sometimes the sidewalks are so long before a cross walk or intersection crossing I am grateful  I have a seat to take a short rest as I walk the distance. Sometimes there are no sidewalks and I must walk on gravel, which is very dangerous or walkway is brick sometimes even cobblestone which are almost always uneven, chipped, raised or broken so gaps that come up quickly and are fall risks.  Weather is always a barrier or CAUTION required to navigate especially, snow, ice, frost, rain or wet from hoses, leaks, sprinklers etc

sidewalkBarriers: One big sidewalk barrier I encounter as a wheelchair user is uneven edges where one sidewalk square is higher than the preceding one, causing the wheelchair to run into the raised edge and potentially tip forward / throw the occupant (me) out if the edge is harsh enough to cause a full stop as opposed to a big bump only. Another sidewalk barrier I encounter in my wheelchair is stationary objects (typically a tree, planter, or pole) residing in the center of the walkway area. While people walking on foot can easily walk around these objects on either side, as a wheelchair user there is almost never enough room for me to pass on either side. This causes me to have to get assistance to get pushed either through a grassy lawn on one side (if this is even an option), or off the high curb and into the street to surpass the obstacle. All of these present major safety risks. One final sidewalk barrier typically seen in front of stores or in downtown areas is large planter pots and signs placed on the sidewalk, which I cannot fit around in my wheelchair. This once again causes me to have to go off the curb and into the street or parking lot to get around the obstacle, before finding another ramped area where I can re-enter the sidewalk. All of these scenarios require me to have someone with me who can assist.
